sec:atomic-braid-mass-intro:
Whereas the nuclear transfer matrices of Transfer Matrices and Beta-Decay Transitions act on the A nucleon strands in H_A(q), a complete neutral atom incorporates Z electron strands braided with the nuclear core inside the enlarged Hecke algebra H_{A+Z}(q). This section extends the linear-programming stability criterion to the full atomic braid and establishes the computational foundations of the Wedderburn atomic mass formula.

The universal integer linear program (ILP), which governs operator selection across quark confinement, nucleon pairing, electron shell attachment, and molecular bonding, here acts on the full atomic braid. Evaluating the symbolic H_3(q) Gram matrix and colour-pairing weights yields an explicit atomic normal-form witness procedure and a step-by-step LP verification pipeline, providing an exact algebraic cross-check for the seven-term q-integer mass formula across Z \le 20.
prop:atomic-lp-stability: Proposition LP stability of the atomic braid. The bare hydrogen atom [e, \mathfrak{p}] = \sigma_0^{-1} in H_2(q) is LP-unstable: there exists a Markov-normalised operator X^* = \alpha \cdot \mathbf{1} + \beta \cdot \sigma_0 that annihilates the traced volume (V = 0).
rem:atomic-lp-stability-dressing:
Remark Borromean dressing and composite-nucleus stabilisation. The \mathcal{B}_3 dressing (proton internal structure) stabilises the atom. The Borromean braid (\sigma_1\sigma_2)^3 is the identity in the standard (degree-2) representation of H_3(q). This changes the annihilation ratio from \lambda_s/\lambda_a = 0.537 (bare) to q^{-10} = 0.352 (dressed). The original annihilator X^* cannot satisfy the dressed condition, so the atom is stable.

For composite nuclei (A \geq 2): nuclear crossings (\mathfrak{p}\mathfrak{p}, \mathfrak{n}\mathfrak{n}, \mathfrak{p}\mathfrak{n}) break the simple H_2(q) structure, providing LP stability without explicit \mathcal{B}_3 dressing.
prop:gram-matrix-h3-symbolic:
Proposition The H_3(q) Hoefsmit-seminormal Gram matrix on the 6-element normal-form basis, with the Markov weight z carried symbolically: its determinant factors so that the canonical weight z = q^3/(q^2+1) is a root, hence the canonical Gram is singular with the three-strand q-antisymmetriser as its radical. Let q > 0 and let z denote the Markov weight, so that on the 6-element Gröbner–Shirshov normal-form basis (b_0, \dots, b_5) = (1, \sigma_0, \sigma_1, \sigma_0\sigma_1, \sigma_1\sigma_0, \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0) of H_3(q) the Markov trace takes the values \mathrm{tr}_M(b_i) = (1, z, z, z^2, z^2, hz^2 + z) with h = q - q^{-1}. Let G(q,z) be the Gram matrix G[i,j] = \mathrm{tr}_M(b_i b_j). Then:

  1. G(q,z) is symmetric and G[0,0] = 1, for every z.

  2. The determinant factors as

  \det G(q,z) \;=\; -\,\frac{(z-q)^5\,(qz+1)^5\,\bigl((q^2+1)z - q^3\bigr)\,
                              (q^3 z + qz + 1)}{q^8}.

  1. At the canonical Markov weight z = q^3/(q^2+1) the third factor vanishes identically in q. Hence \det G = 0 for every q; the form has rank 5, and its radical is spanned by (-q^3,\, q^2,\, q^2,\, -q,\, -q,\, 1) — the three-strand q-antisymmetriser \sum_i (-q^{-1})^{\ell_i} b_i up to scale, where \ell_i is the word length of b_i. In particular G is not positive definite.

  2. Away from the four roots z \in \{q, -q^{-1}, q^3/(q^2+1), -1/(q^3+q)\}, \det G(q,z) \neq 0 identically; thus the vanishing in item 3 is a specific property of the two-row Markov root z = q^3/(q^2+1) rather than a formal identity in z.
rem:gram-matrix-h3-symbolic-eval-role: Remark Numerical evaluation and role of the symbolic H_3(q) Gram matrix.
rem:color-pairing-binding:
Remark Degree-2 color pairing as binding energy. The color-tube cubic c^3 + a_2 c^2 + a_1 c + a_0 = 0 generates four distinct terms. These map exactly to the four photon channels in \gamma\gamma \to \mathfrak{q}\mathfrak{q}\mathfrak{q} production:

Degree Symmetric function Integral Physical role
3 \prod \mathrm{d}c_k/\mathrm{d}z I_3 confinement \to m_{\mathfrak{p}}
2 \sum_{i<j} \mathrm{d}c_i \cdot \mathrm{d}c_j I_2 color pairing \to binding
1 \sum \mathrm{d}c_k/\mathrm{d}z I_1 quark sum
0 c_0 + z I_0 electron period

The degree-2 amplification ratio A_2/A_3 rigidly fixes the weight \beta_2 = -2[3]_q in the mass formula. The quantum 3-integer [3]_q emerges because the baryon carries three color channels. The pairwise color interaction is initially weighted by the classical pair count \binom{3}{2} = 3, which resolves to [3]_q at finite q.
prop:atomic-nf-witness:
Proposition Atomic braid normal form witness. For each atom (Z, N) with Z = 1--20, the atomic braid construction produces an element of H_{A+Z}(q) that is verified to be in Gröbner--Shirshov normal form. Specifically:

  1. The ground-state nucleon ordering is the global minimum of \Phi_1 over all \binom{A}{Z} permutations.
  2. Each electron is inserted at the position minimizing \Phi_1.
sec:atomic-braid-mass-crossing-locality-: On the composite atomic braid H_{A+Z}(q), the crossing-graded mass expansion is constrained by local holonomy and discrete spacetime symmetries. This section derives q-holonomy locality from the graded connection on the Reeb bundle, proves that the CPT orbit closure is dense in the unitary representation fibre, and establishes the closure of the discrete symmetries C, P, T—deriving time-reversal invariance T from trace cyclicity \mathrm{tr}_M(ab) = \mathrm{tr}_M(ba), reading parity P as the mirror reflection of the braid diagram, and obtaining parity/charge-conjugation from Type-B crystal folding. Proving invariance of the atomic mass functional under the Lusztig bar involution q \mapsto q^{-1} secures real-valuedness of the binding energy and characterizes the soft-confinement regime at q_0.
rem:q-holonomy-locality-derivation: Remark Derivation: locality from flatness of the KZ connection.
conj:cpt-orbit-closure-density:
Conjecture CPT-saturation as Type-B fold-orbit closure: deriving \rho_F \in \{m_e, 2m_e\} from crystal structure. Let \sigma \colon \mathrm{Part}(n) \to \mathrm{Part}(n) be the transpose involution. Define \mathrm{CPTSat}(\mathcal{K}) to mean \Lambda(\mathcal{K}) is closed under the fold.

Then the Frobenius packing-density rule is a derived consequence of crystal structure:

  \boxed{\;
    \rho_F(\mathcal{K})
    \;=\;
    \begin{cases}
      m_e   & \text{if } \mathrm{CPTSat}(\mathcal{K}) \text{ is false}, \\[4pt]
      2 m_e & \text{if } \mathrm{CPTSat}(\mathcal{K}) \text{ is true}.
    \end{cases}
  \;}
conj:cpt-d6-d7-d8-closure:
Conjecture CPT closure: charge conjugation, parity and time reversal jointly preserve the Markov trace. The three discrete symmetries close consistently: there exist actions C, P, T on closed-braid representatives of H_n(q) such that

  1. C is the color-sheet flavor-swap u \leftrightarrow \bar u, d \leftrightarrow \bar d;
  2. P is the braid-diagram mirror reflection, or writhe sign flip;
  3. T is the Markov-trace word reversal, or trace-cyclicity dual.

The composite C \cdot P \cdot T preserves the Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M \colon H_n(q) \to R. That is, \mathrm{tr}_M((C \cdot P \cdot T)\beta) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta) for every closed-braid representative \beta.

The joint statement is that they compose to the CPT theorem at the Markov-trace level. The three components are not logically independent; they collectively constitute the conjecture. Only the components are conjectural: if each of C, P and T preserves \mathrm{tr}_M, so does their composite, so the joint statement reduces to the three component conjectures. Each component asserts that the named realisation of its symmetry is trace-preserving, and none is proved.

The conjecture is stated over the closed-braid space B, the trace \mathrm{tr} and the CPT action \mathrm{cpt} it concerns. Downstream results that require CPT closure take it as an explicit hypothesis. Here R is the coefficient ring of the trace—canonically \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}], with an archimedean evaluation R := \mathbb{R} arising only on the observation side of the substrate–archimedean wall.
conj:t-from-trace-cyclicity:
Conjecture Time-reversal T as Markov-trace word reversal (trace cyclicity dual). Within the QOU framework, time-reversal T acts as word reversal on braid words at the Markov-trace level:

  T \;:\;
  \sigma_{i_1}^{\epsilon_1} \cdots \sigma_{i_\ell}^{\epsilon_\ell}
  \;\longmapsto\;
  \sigma_{i_\ell}^{\epsilon_\ell} \cdots \sigma_{i_1}^{\epsilon_1}.

By the Markov trace cyclicity axiom \mathrm{tr}_M(ab) = \mathrm{tr}_M(ba), word reversal is trace-invariant for the Markov closure. The Jones polynomial of K and of its time-reversed counterpart K^T coincide. The operator T is an involution (T^2 = \mathrm{id}). It preserves q, color-sheet flavors, and Hecke generator signs. It acts purely on the ordering of crossings.

For a braid word \beta, define \beta^T as the reversed word. Trace cyclicity gives \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta^T). The reversed word produces the mirror-orientation link, which has the same Jones polynomial as the original. T alone is the trace-cyclicity dual. Composed with C and P, it recovers the bar-involution = CPT composite.
conj:p-from-braid-mirror:
Conjecture Parity P as mirror reflection of the braid diagram (writhe sign flip). Within the QOU framework, parity P acts as the mirror reflection of the braid diagram — each positive crossing \sigma_i \mapsto \sigma_i^{-1} and vice versa, with the q-parameter held fixed (q \mapsto q, not q \mapsto q^{-1}). Equivalently, P negates the signed writhe w(K) \mapsto -w(K) of every braid word. P is an involution (P^2 = \mathrm{id}) and is distinct from:

  • the bar-involution Bar-involution and its P_{\mathrm{avg}} / P_{\mathrm{skew}} projections, which acts as q \mapsto q^{-1} AND \sigma_i \mapsto \sigma_i^{-1} simultaneously (= composite CPT);
  • charge conjugation Charge conjugation C as the color-sheet flavor-swap u \leftrightarrow \bar u, d \leftrightarrow \bar d, which acts on color-sheet flavor labels with no Hecke- generator action;
  • time-reversal Time-reversal T as Markov-trace word reversal (trace cyclicity dual), which reverses the braid word at the Markov-trace level.
conj:type-b-folding-cpt:
Conjecture Type-B Coxeter folding realises CPT via Hecke-algebra \mathbb{Z}/2 fixed points. The involution \iota: s_i \leftrightarrow s_{n-i} of the Coxeter diagram folds the Weyl group S_n into a Coxeter group of type \mathrm{B}_{\lfloor n/2 \rfloor} (of type \mathrm{A}_1 at n = 3), and the canonical atomic-braid Hecke algebra H_n(q) folds to the Hecke algebra of that group with the weight function below, in Lusztig's quasisplit sense [lusztig2003, Sec. 16.2]. The folded algebra carries the bar involution and canonical basis of this weight function, and its GS normal forms are bar-involution invariant by construction. Stable matter = the elements of H_n(q) fixed by the algebra involution \theta(\sigma_i) = \sigma_{n-i} that lifts \iota; antimatter = the elements \theta moves. Under this folding, the composite CPT operator decomposes naturally as a tensor of:

  • C from color-sheet flavor conjugation
  • P from Type-B Coxeter folding, in role only: the fold \theta permutes the letters and keeps their eigenvalues, so it does not have the profile of P defined below
  • T from Markov-trace cyclicity

Type-B folding provides an alternative categorical realisation where the role of "P (braid mirror)" is replaced by "the Coxeter-fold Z/2", and the bar-invariance emerges from the folded Hecke algebra rather than from explicit \sigma_{i} \leftrightarrow \sigma_{i}^{-1} braid manipulation. The Type-B folding view is more compact but requires more category theory.

Rank and generator weights. The statement is made at the level of Coxeter groups and Hecke algebras for every n. For odd n = 2m+1 the corresponding fold of the \mathfrak{sl}_n Cartan datum would put the adjacent roots \alpha_m, \alpha_{m+1} in one orbit, so the conjecture makes no claim about Cartan data. The rank is the number of \iota-orbits on the n-1 simple reflections, which is \lfloor n/2 \rfloor. At the level of Coxeter groups this is Lusztig's quasisplit case: with s_i the simple reflection of \alpha_i, the \iota-fixed subgroup of S_n is a Coxeter group generated by the longest elements of the \iota-orbits, and the folded Hecke algebra carries the weight function given by their ambient lengths [lusztig2003, Sec. 16.2]. The two parities differ only at the middle of the diagram. For even n the middle root \alpha_{n/2} is fixed, so its generator s_{n/2} has weight 1; the other generators s_i s_{n-i} have weight 2. For odd n = 2m+1 the middle roots \alpha_m and \alpha_{m+1} are adjacent and form one orbit, so its generator is s_m s_{m+1} s_m of weight 3; at n = 3 this is the whole folded group, of type \mathrm{A}_1. For n \ge 4 the weights are unequal, so the folded algebra is a Hecke algebra with unequal parameters. With the ambient parameter equal to q, as for H_n(q), these are q^2 on the generators s_i s_{n-i} and q or q^3 on the middle generator. The fold is not an algebra map that sends each folded generator to the product of its ambient generators: for a swapped pair, \sigma_i \sigma_{n-i} has the three eigenvalues q^2, -1 and q^{-2}, while a Hecke generator of weight 2 has two.

On the type-B side the Markov traces are classified: there is exactly one for each parameter z and each sequence (y_k)_{k\ge 1} of values on the elements t_0't_1'\cdots t_{k-1}', and each restricts to Ocneanu's trace on the type-A subalgebra [geck-lambropoulou-2004, Def. 4.1, Thm. 4.3]. Which of these traces the T factor uses is not fixed by the conjecture.

Scope at fixed q. Three involutions send a Hecke letter \sigma_i to a letter: \sigma_i \mapsto \sigma_i^{-1}, \sigma_i \mapsto -\sigma_i^{-1} and \sigma_i \mapsto -\sigma_i. They form a Klein four-group, the composite of any two being the third. Let P_+ and P_- be the idempotents of \sigma_i for its eigenvalues q and -q^{-1}, and let e^- = \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 with mirror e^+ = \sigma_0^{-1}\sigma_1^{-1}\sigma_0^{-1}, as in the Breit–Wheeler vertex. The braid mirror \sigma_i \mapsto \sigma_i^{-1} keeps P_+ and P_- and sends e^- to e^+, which is the profile of C (of CT if q \mapsto q^{-1} is read as antilinear). The map \sigma_i \mapsto -\sigma_i^{-1} exchanges P_+ and P_- and sends e^- to -e^+, which is the profile of CP. Only \sigma_i \mapsto -\sigma_i has the profile of P: it exchanges P_+ and P_- and sends e^- to -e^-.

Neither \sigma_i \mapsto \sigma_i^{-1} nor \sigma_i \mapsto -\sigma_i is realised by an algebra map of H_n(q) that is linear over the scalars, unless q^2 = 1. Both exist only as maps covering q \mapsto q^{-1} on the scalars, and that map has no counterpart at the real substrate value q_0. Hence no letter-level map has the profile of P at fixed real q. The fold \theta(\sigma_i) = \sigma_{n-i} is not of this kind either. It keeps q fixed and sends the idempotents of \sigma_i for q and -q^{-1} to those of \sigma_{n-i} for the same eigenvalues, so it exchanges no P_+ with a P_-. The conjecture's claim is therefore narrower: \theta takes the place of P in the decomposition above, without having its profile.
prop:bar-involution-invariance:
Proposition Bar-involution invariance of Plancherel weights and Type-B-folded normal forms. (Conditional.) Let \bar\cdot be the bar-involution sending q \mapsto q^{-1}. Then:

  1. (Plancherel-weight invariance) The Plancherel weight satisfies \overline{w_\lambda(q)} = w_\lambda(q).
  2. (Transpose-pair equality) w_\lambda(q) = w_{\lambda^T}(q).
  3. (Type-B-folded normal forms) Any Hecke normal form produced by the pair-production engine is bar-invariant: \overline{T_w} = T_w.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the substrate wall.
rem:bar-involution-invariance-significan: Remark Significance of bar-involution invariance as a witness test.
prop:mirror-baseline-cancellation:
Proposition Mirror-pair cancellation of the bar-even binding baseline. Let (Z, N) and (N, Z) be a mirror pair at fixed mass number A = Z + N, with crossing statistics of the atomic braid word

\sigma + \sigma^{-1} = 10A - 2, \qquad \mathrm{avg} = 2A + 1, \qquad w = \sigma - \sigma^{-1} = 4Z.

Then the two bar-even statistics are mirror-invariant, (\sigma+\sigma^{-1})(Z,N) = (\sigma+\sigma^{-1})(N,Z) and \mathrm{avg}(Z,N) = \mathrm{avg}(N,Z), while the bar-odd writhe is the unique distinguishing crossing statistic:

w(Z,N) - w(N,Z) = 4(Z - N).

Consequently, for any binding-exponent deviation of the additive form f(Z,N) = \beta(A) + \zeta(Z-N) separating an A-dependent bar-even baseline \beta(A) from an interface-imbalance functional \zeta(Z-N), the mirror difference cancels the baseline identically:

f(Z,N) - f(N,Z) = \zeta(Z-N) - \zeta(N-Z).
prop:isovector-chiral-residue:
Proposition Binding isovector coefficient as the W_\lambda chiral residue (conditional). Conditional on the identification BWVacuumRowIsHecke. Let the bar-odd isovector component of the nuclear binding residual equal the chiral residue of the W_\lambda Plancherel measure \mu(\lambda) = d_q(\lambda)^2/D^2—that is, the Reeb-involution-odd chiral mass component \mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{chiral}} (Chirality residue mass term, Archimedean chirality) coupled to the isovector writhe 2(Z-N) (Mirror-pair cancellation of the bar-even binding baseline) with chiral weight \kappa. Then the isovector mirror difference satisfies

b(Z,N) - b(N,Z) \;=\; 4\,\kappa\,(Z-N),

independently of the mass number A = Z+N; equivalently, the per-isospin slope b = 4\kappa is determined without free parameters by the single chiral weight \kappa.
rem:soft-confinement-at-q0:
Remark Soft confinement level \ell_*(q_0) from Plancherel decay. 1. Soft confinement at the substrate parameter. The Wedderburn block labels of H_n(q) are q-independent, but the Plancherel weights depend sensitively on q. At roots of unity, sharp truncation occurs. At the generic real substrate parameter q_0 \approx 1.11, no representation is strictly confined, but weights decay rapidly, producing a soft confinement level \ell_*(q_0) \approx 9.6. Partitions exceeding \ell_* contribute negligibly.

2. Implication for atomic braids. An atomic braid lives in H_{3A}(q_0). Soft confinement implies no truncation for light atoms, exponential suppression for medium atoms, and effective truncation for heavy atoms. This transition dictates why \alpha-cluster unfolding is numerically necessary beyond A \sim 4.

3. Numerical estimate. See Table. The rapid saturation demonstrates soft confinement. The cutoff \ell_*(q_0) \approx 10 is the horizon where grading effectively terminates.

sec:branching-qvalue-intro:
While the Wedderburn atomic mass formula determines total ground-state masses, predicting individual \beta^-, \beta^+, and electron-capture decay endpoints requires isolating the single active nucleon channel from the remaining A-1 spectator nucleons. Under the wreath-product branching S_3^A \subset S_{3A}, the composite trace factors into an active conversion channel multiplied by a normalized spectator background.

This section defines the per-nucleon channel decomposition and spectator normalization, proves the branching \mathcal{Q}_q-value factorisation theorem, and shows that the parity of the mass number A selects the active pairing regime. Incorporating the positron branch shift and the Frobenius positivity filter yields the symbolic tritium \mathcal{Q}_q-value, the categorical quantity dictionary, and the proof that the Borromean link \mathcal{B}_3 is a strict local minimum of the categorical action on the Temperley–Lieb quotient.
def:per-nucleon-channel-decomposition:
Definition Per-nucleon channel decomposition via S_3^A branching. The per-nucleon channel decomposition of the typed Garside element for a nucleus of mass number A is the factorization

  G(c_1, \ldots, c_A)
  = \prod_{m=1}^{A} G_{n_m}(c_m),

where each per-nucleon factor G_{n_m}(c_m) is the expectation value of \Delta_3 in the T_{2,3} eigenvector of channel c_m, n_m \in \{P, N\} is the nucleon type, and c_m \in \{\mathrm{triv}, \mathrm{conf}, \mathrm{unconf}, \mathrm{sign}\} ranges over the four channels of the T_{2,3} eigenstructure of H_3(q).

rem:per-nucleon-channel-decomposition-re:
Remark Branching origin and channels of the per-nucleon decomposition. S_3^A branching.

The typed Garside element acts on V^{\otimes 3A}. The S_3^A branching rule decomposes this action into a product of A per-nucleon factors.

Four channels from the T_{2,3} eigendecomposition.

The trefoil operator T_{2,3} = \sigma_0 \sigma_1 \sigma_0 in H_3(q) has four eigenvalues corresponding to four channels:

  1. Trivial (\lambda = q^3): fully symmetric channel
  2. Confining (\lambda = q^{-1}): standard representation, confining component
  3. Unconfining (\lambda = -q): standard representation, anti-confining component
  4. Sign (\lambda = -q^{-3}): fully antisymmetric channel
def:spectator-normalization:
Definition Spectator normalization factor. The spectator normalization factor of a beta decay with Z protons and N - 1 spectator neutrons is

  S(Z, N-1) = a^{Z} \cdot b^{N-1}

where a = -h/2 and b = -3(q^2-1)(q^2+1)^2/(4q^3) are the channel sums of the per-nucleon Garside factors.
rem:spectator-normalization-remark:
Remark Origin and sign of the spectator normalization. The spectator normalization captures the contribution of unchanged nucleons to the Q-value character sum. In a beta decay, one neutron converts to a proton. The remaining Z protons and N - 1 neutrons act as spectators.

Fermionic character. Both a < 0 and b < 0 for all q > 1. This negativity reflects the fermionic character of the nucleon. The sign of the spectator product is (-1)^{A-1}. This sign fixes the parity regime for the Q-value.
prop:branching-qvalue-factorization: Proposition Exact factorization of the branching Q-value. Compute the branching \mathcal{Q}_q-value by summing over all 4^A channel configurations.
prf:branching-qvalue-factorization:
Proof Proof of branching qvalue factorization. The full character sum distributes over the product structure of the per-nucleon decomposition:

  \sum_{c_1, \ldots, c_A}
  \Bigl(\prod_{m=1}^{A} G_{n'_m}(c_m)
        - \prod_{m=1}^{A} G_{n_m}(c_m)\Bigr)

where n'_m is the daughter nucleon type (the changed nucleon switches N \to P; all others are unchanged). The sum over c_m factors independently for each nucleon:

  = \Bigl(\prod_{\text{spectator } P} a\Bigr)
    \cdot \Bigl(\prod_{\text{spectator } N} b\Bigr)
    \cdot (a - b)
  = a^Z \cdot b^{N-1} \cdot (a - b)

The factorization is exact. The only inputs are the eight per-nucleon channel values G_P(c) and G_N(c), which are rational functions of q.
thm:parity-regime-selection: Theorem Parity regime selection for Q-values. The parity of the mass number A fixes the sign of the spectator factor in the branching Q-value factorization.
prf:parity-regime-selection:
Proof Proof of parity regime selection. Write a = -a' and b = -b' with a', b' > 0, and N = M + 1. Then A - 1 = Z + M and

  (-1)^{Z+M}\, a^Z\, b^{M} = (-1)^{Z+M}(-1)^{Z}(-1)^{M}\, a'^Z\, b'^M = a'^Z\, b'^M > 0,

since (-1)^{2(Z+M)} = 1. \square
rem:parity-regime-dispatch:
Remark Parity regime dispatch for Q-values. The sign identity is used to select one of three Q-value formulas. The selection is a per-case prescription; none of the three formulas is derived.

  1. Odd A (A \geq 3): the factorization a^Z b^{N-1}(a-b) is positive, and the prescription is Q = |S \cdot \Delta| \times m_e.
  2. Even A: the factorization is negative. The prescription restricts the sum to Frobenius-positive configurations (confinement LP) and takes Q = (\Sigma_{\mathrm{FP}} + 1) \times m_e.
  3. A = 1 (neutron decay): there are no spectators, and the prescription adds the positron correction, Q = (S\Delta + 1) \times m_e.

The comparison of a against b is fixed: a - b = (q^2-1)\bigl(3(q^2+1)^2 - 2q^2\bigr)/(4q^3) > 0 for q > 1, so |b| > |a|.
prop:positron-correction: Proposition Parity-dependent Q-value offset. The +1 additive term in the Q-value formula is a parity-dependent offset \delta_A, required to match the evaluated character sum to the observed kinematics.
prop:tritium-qvalue-symbolic: Proposition Symbolic Q-value for tritium beta decay. The Q-value for tritium beta decay {}^3\mathrm{H} \to {}^3\mathrm{He} + e^- + \bar\nu_e admits an exact closed form as a rational function of q.
prop:frobenius-positivity-filter:
Proposition Frobenius positivity filter for even-A decays. For even A: a channel configuration is Frobenius-positive if and only if both parent and daughter yield non-negative Markov traces.

A configuration is excluded exactly when its sign-pattern has odd total parity. Of the 2^A sign-patterns, exactly half are excluded.
rem:frobenius-positivity-filter-context: Remark Motivation, LP connection, and the {}^6\mathrm{He} worked count for the Frobenius filter. For nuclei with even mass number A, the raw character sum is negative. The physical Q-value is obtained by restricting the sum to Frobenius-positive configurations.
rem:categorical-quantity-map:
Remark Categorical quantity map: mass, Q-value, decay rate, density. The four principal physical observables correspond rigidly to four distinct functionals acting on the categorical action:

Physical quantity Categorical functional Formula
Mass Markov trace (absolute value) \mathfrak{m} = \vert \mathrm{tr}_M(\Phi)\vert
Q-value Character sum Q = \sum_\lambda \chi_\lambda(\Delta) \times m_e
Decay rate Frobenius matrix element \mathfrak{D} \propto \vert \langle v, \Phi v \rangle_F\vert ^2
Density Partial trace (crossing count) \rho = \mathrm{tr}_A(\varrho)

Each functional isolates an orthogonal dimension of the underlying Hecke algebra element.
rem:b3-local-minimum: Remark \mathcal{B}_3 is a local minimum of the categorical action. The Borromean braid \mathcal{B}_3 = (\sigma_0 \sigma_1^{-1})^3 is shown to be a local, rather than global, minimum of the categorical action.
prose:intro-pair-production-anyon:
In the Kashiwara crystal limit, pair creation \gamma\gamma \to e^+e^- is a categorical anyon-collapse transition. Two photons \gamma(\varphi), \gamma(\psi) \in H_3(R, q), each of the form 1 + \varphi_0\sigma_0 + \varphi_1\sigma_1 + \varphi_{01}\,\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1}, meet at a Type-B folded crystal fixed point. Its involutive symmetry projects onto a conjugate particle–antiparticle pair: the electron word \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 \in B_3 (closure: the Hopf link) and its bar conjugate \sigma_0^{-1}\sigma_1^{-1}\sigma_0^{-1}.

This section formulates the symmetric-crystal pair-production mechanism and the two-photon Breit–Wheeler vertex, defines the anyonic Hecke substrate, proves modular tensor category (MTC) truncation at roots of unity and the Kazhdan–Lusztig classical limit q \to 1, and establishes the observation-induced collapse of anyonic braid superpositions onto definite charge eigenstates.
conj:symmetric-crystal-pair-production:
Conjecture Type-B folding forces matter/antimatter to be created in conjugate-operator pairs. Let H_n(R, q) be the Iwahori–Hecke algebra of type A_{n-1} with Hecke normal forms \{T_w\}. Let \mathrm{Cryst}(\mathfrak{sl}_n) be its associated Kashiwara crystal. Fold the \mathfrak{sl}_n Cartan datum into a Type B Cartan datum along the Dynkin involution i \mapsto \bar i = n - i. Equivalently, apply the \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z} bar-involution T_w \mapsto \overline{T_w} that sends q \mapsto q^{-1} and reverses crossings. The resulting symmetric crystal \mathrm{Cryst}^{\mathrm{sym}}(\mathfrak{so}_{2n+1}) admits no Kashiwara lowering operator \tilde f_i as a unimodal step from a bar-invariant source. Every step is a paired operator (\tilde f_i, \tilde f_{\bar i}). Consequently, a transition

  v_0 \;\xrightarrow{\;(\tilde f_i, \tilde f_{\bar i})\;}\; v_-\,\sqcup\,v_+,

from a bar-invariant highest-weight vector v_0 produces two descendants v_-, v_+ whose Hecke normal forms are bar-conjugates (\overline{T_{v_-}} = T_{v_+}). Identify v_- with a chiral particle and v_+ with its CPT antiparticle. The symmetric crystal forbids the production of a single chiral excitation from a non-chiral source. Any descendant set is a disjoint union of bar-conjugate pairs.

Algorithmic role (charge-conservation kill switch). The Gröbner–Shirshov reduction engine enforces matter–antimatter pairing structurally. At each crystal step, it applies the folded operator pair atomically. An internally generated intermediate carrying a single net chirality is unreachable. The Hecke normal forms produced by the engine are bar-invariant by construction. The engine rejects any candidate normal form failing this test before further expansion. This converts CPT and charge conservation from combinatorial post-conditions into intrinsic invariants of the crystal traversal. No custom \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z} rules are required.

Conjectural status. The Type B folding of \mathfrak{sl}_n Kashiwara crystals into \mathfrak{so}_{2n+1} symmetric crystals is established at the level of generic quantum-group representations. The bar-involution is intrinsic to the KLR canonical basis. The conjecture is that the folded operators on the cyclotomic quotient realising H_n(R, q) realise exactly the matter/antimatter pairing of the topological ansatz. The bar-conjugate pair on a single Type B crystal node corresponds to a CPT pair of QOU particles. The empirical evidence is the \det \rho_\lambda(w) \cdot \det \rho_{\lambda'}(w) = \pm 1 identity for every conjugate-partition pair (\lambda, \lambda'). This identity is the bar-involution acting on Wedderburn blocks.
